title: Pin a notice to a tilted display board with its top edge at the line
instruction: Pin the notice to the display board with its top edge at the line, then let go.
context: Teaching assistants put up notices on cork display boards (O*NET 25-9042 Teaching Assistants, Except Postsecondary, 1.46 million employed: "Prepare lesson materials, bulletin board displays, exhibits, equipment, and demonstrations"). On a tilted or upright board the notice slides down unless one hand holds it where it should go while the other pushes a pushpin through it into the cork, square to the board and hard enough to take.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); the layout is the same in every trial. (1) A cork display board on a desk easel (a tabletop easel rather than a wall board, so the face is within the arms' reach; its slope still makes the notice slide, which is what forces the hold), fixed: cork face 30 up the face by 32 across and 1.2 thick, tilted 30 degrees from the table (face up and toward the arms), its low edge at x 12, 3 above the table, spanning y -10 to +22; a wooden ledge 1 x 32 x 1.2 along the low edge, standing 1.2 proud of the face; a pine foot 3 x 32 x 3 and a pine rear strut 3 x 3 hold it. Two black ticks 2 long and 2 mm wide, 1.2 in from each side of the face, mark the line 17.5 up the face from the ledge. (2) A laminated A6 notice, white, 14.8 x 10.5 x 0.1, 6 g, lying flat on the face and standing on the ledge, centred at y 7 (it spans y 1.75 to 12.25); its top edge is 15 up the face, 2.5 below the line. (3) A pushpin, 5 g: red plastic head 11 mm tall and 9 to 11 mm across over an 11 mm collar, and an 8 mm steel needle; it stands needle-down in a pin cup (a grey plastic block 4 x 4 x 2 with a 3 mm hole, fixed) at x 25, y -17, its collar resting on the cup.
scoring: Judged at the end, with a ruler. 0.25: the pushpin stands in the cork (at least 2 mm in, anywhere on the board) and has been let go (credit for taking the pin and driving it in). 0.5: its needle is through the notice at least 3 mm from the notice's edges, its head seated on it (within 1.5 mm), and let go, but the notice is not at the line or hangs crooked. 0.75: the notice is pinned like that with its top edge within 1 cm of the line and its long edges within 5 degrees of the board's up direction, but a gripper's fingertip centre is still within 3 cm of the board face or 4 cm of the pin. 1.0: as 0.75 with both grippers clear and the notice still (its top edge has moved under 2 mm and it has turned under 1 degree in the last 0.5 s), held for 2 s; the trial then ends. 0 otherwise, including a notice that has come off the board.
reset_notes: Pull the pushpin out and stand it needle-down in the cup; take the notice off and stand it on the ledge, centred on its mark (y 7, its top edge 2.5 below the line). Each trial leaves a pinhole in the cork and the notice; swap the notice after about ten trials.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (Isaac Sim/PhysX, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control). The cork is a resistance model: the needle sits on a slider in the pin's head with 6 N of friction, so a push over 6 N drives the pin in, and a pin left in the cork is held fixed by it (pulling it out again isn't modelled). The needle through the notice is a pivot: the notice turns about the pin but can't slide off it. The notice is a rigid laminated card. Friction: cork 0.3, pads on the card 1.0. The 6 N is an estimate.
